notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on several points and the story says so where it matters. (1) Purchase year: the register says 1980, CLUI says 1981. (2) Departure: the register says the followers left in the 1990s; CLUI says the property was vacated after the Bhagwan's 1985 deportation and sold at auction in 1988. (3) Design and height: the register describes a two-story ground house; firelookout.com gives a six-foot wooden tower with a 14-by-14-foot cab. The record's height_m 4.3 m equals 14 ft, which matches the cab dimension rather than a height. No reliable height was found, so height_m is not repeated in facts and a human should review the record's value. (4) Elevation: the record and register give 2,654 ft (809 m); firelookout.com and the directory give 4,040 ft. Not resolved. (5) Coordinates: the register gives 44.91068, -120.7228; firelookout.org's Oregon list gives 44.83310, -120.62426, roughly 11 km apart by my arithmetic. Not resolved, and the record keeps the register's point. (6) Staffing: the register says the lookout stands empty; the directory says Unknown. Story uses unstaffed, undated. The brief's 'shares a register number' note: a FFLOS record for the Sandy Sod Tower Site in Pennsylvania also carries US 471 (FFLOS numbering), so the collision is between two different towers in different registers. The merge report also flags this tower's coordinates as a far match to the Oregon list (register_match_far). Access: no public access is stated; the story advises against visiting. Photo: firelookout.com credits Debbie Newell; licence and image URL not found, so no photo added. The CLUI page covers the wider Rajneeshpuram site and does not mention this lookout by name. Verification 2026-10-08: the story now attributes the built-from-scratch description to Rajneeshpuram (the CLUI subject), says the Center ties the vacating to the 1985 deportation rather than placing it after, and footnotes the 1991 sale and the coordinate difference. Events for the 1980/1981 purchase, 1985 deportation, 1988 auction, 1990s departure, 1991 sale and 1996 donation were added so the timeline matches the story.
